title: WHOIS-style text and registration fields
intro: Work from the module directory. Parse **`whois_sample.txt`** only.

questions.prompt: Print every line from **`whois_sample.txt`** that identifies the **registrar** of the domain.
Print **only** the FQDN from the **`Domain Name:`** record (no label, no leading spaces).
How many field values have been withheld for **privacy** in this record? Print **only** the integer.
Print all **nameserver** entries from the record (full lines, file order).
questions.expectedOutput:
Name Server: NS2.LAB-DNS.EXAMPLE.TEST
Name Server: NS1.LAB-DNS.EXAMPLE.TEST
Name Server: NS2.LAB-DNS.EXAMPLE.TEST

questions.prompt: Print **only** the email from the **`abuse-mailbox:`** attribute in the inetnum-style section (one line, no key).
Find and print the domain **status** line indicating the domain is locked against transfers.
Print **only** the ISO timestamp from **`Creation Date:`** (value after the colon), e.g. **`2019-03-01T08:00:00Z`**.
Print the line that specifies the **IP address range** of the network block covered by this record.
From every **`Name Server:`** line, extract the hostname (after the colon), then print **unique** hostnames **sorted** (ASCII), **one per line**.
Print **only** the human-readable string from the **`org-name:`** attribute (no key).

summaryMarkdown:
## Learning outcomes

- Query domain vs IP WHOIS with correct server selection (`whois -h` where supported) when you have authorization and a throttled workflow.
- Parse common fields (registrar, abuse contact, inetnum, name servers, org identity) from **saved** text with `grep` / `sed` / `sort` / `awk`, without automating bulk scraping irresponsibly.
- Understand RDAP as modern JSON alternative to port-43 WHOIS.

## Scope

**In scope:** manual/slow CLI usage, parsing saved outputs in `/home/isopod/labs/25-whois-registration-data/`. **Out of scope:** bulk IP ownership databases (`Team Cymru`, MaxMind) beyond pointers.

## Concept outline

1. **`whois` client** — recursion to registrar servers; thin vs thick registry models (concept).
2. **IP allocations** — inetnum, netname, abuse-mailbox field importance.
3. **Rate limiting** — why scripts sleep; some RIRs block aggressive clients.
4. **Privacy/redaction** — GDPR-style WHOIS redaction impact on investigations.
5. **RDAP** — `curl` JSON from RDAP bootstrap (**19**); `jwhois` legacy.

## Tooling and alternatives

| Task | Primary | Alternatives |
|------|---------|----------------|
| Port 43 WHOIS | `whois` | `jwhois`, `rwlookup` wrappers; web UI in browser (out of CLI scope). |
| RDAP | `curl` + `jq` | `rdap` CLI tools if packaged; `whois` some builds speak RDAP hybrid. |
| ASN / BGP view | N/A | `whois -h whois.radb.net`, `bgpq4` for IRR filters; `asnmap` style tools — advanced sidebar. |
| Geolocation | N/A | `geoiplookup` (MaxMind legacy), online APIs — consent/rate. |
